name: Independence Dam State Park
governance: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Parks and Watercraft
description: Located on the banks of the Maumee River, the park features ruins of the Miami and Erie Canal and a three-mile hiking trail following the historic canal towpath that meanders between the old canal and the river through a dense hardwood forest. Over 200 bird species have been recorded. The park is along the Maumee State Scenic River.
location: 27722 County Rd 424, Defiance, Ohio 43512; approximately 3 miles east of Defiance on the Maumee River
features: Camping;Boat Ramp;Marina;Pavilion;Hiking Trail;Restrooms;Fire Ring;Picnic Area;Historic Lock
notes: NCT/Buckeye Trail routes through park along canal towpath. CONFIRM: 25 vs 40 primitive campsites (sources conflict). NID baseline seed 'Independence Dam (NID)' resolves to park infrastructure, not separate entity.

name: Oxbow Lake Wildlife Area
governance: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Wildlife
description: Located in the glaciated lake plain of northwestern Ohio with slightly rolling topography. Mud Creek bisects the area, featuring large cottonwoods and sycamores along its banks, while upland woods consist mostly of oaks and hickories. Substantial areas of brushland and meadow are maintained for upland game habitat. Ohio purchased the originally forested land in 1948 after it had been cleared for farming in the previous century.
location: Defiance County, Ohio; near Defiance, Bryan, and Napoleon
features: Boat Ramp;Parking Lot;Hiking Trail;Fishing Area;ADA Accessible
notes: Contains Big Oxbow Lake (38 ac) and Little Oxbow Lake (4.5 ac). Flag DEF-F-06: 'western agreement parcel' — no evidence found; UNRESOLVED. NID 'Oxbow Lake Dam' resolves to infrastructure, not separate entity. Fishing: northern pike, largemouth bass, bluegills, bullheads.

name: Winchester's Camp No. 3 / Fort Starvation
governance: Ohio Department of Natural Resources
description: War of 1812 winter encampment site (Nov. 2, 1812 – Jan. 1, 1813) for three Kentucky Militia Regiments and one regiment of US Regulars under Colonel Wells, stationed approximately six miles below Fort Winchester on the north bank of the Maumee River. Nicknamed 'Fort Starvation' by soldiers due to supply shortages. Believed burial site of approximately 300 Kentucky soldiers; thousands of bones were disturbed when the Miami and Erie Canal was dug through the burial ground (1837–1848) and reinterred. Historical marker erected 2010 by Defiance County Chapter Ohio Genealogical Society and other organizations.
location: Four miles east of the City of Defiance on US Route 424 on the bank of the Maumee River, within Independence Dam State Park
notes: ODNR Historic Site #24. Also known as 'Old Kentucky Burial Grounds.' Child site within Independence Dam State Park (DEF-S-001). GPS propagated from parent site.

governance: Defiance Soil and Water Conservation District

name: Auglaize Village
governance: Defiance County Historical Society
description: A living history village founded in 1966 by the Defiance County Historical Society that preserves the history of the men and women who carved a community out of the Great Black Swamp, featuring restored and reconstructed 19th-century buildings, farm museums, and multiple specialty museums.

name: Fort Grounds
governance: City of Defiance, Parks & Recreation Department
description: The Fort Grounds occupy the site of Fort Defiance, erected by General Anthony Wayne in 1794 at the confluence of the Maumee and Auglaize Rivers during his campaign leading to the Battle of Fallen Timbers. Points in the sidewalk memorialize the corners of the fort. The grounds have been preserved for over a century since the city's incorporation. The Defiance Public Library (Carnegie Library) is also located on the grounds.
location: 320 Fort Street, Defiance, OH 43512; at the confluence of the Maumee and Auglaize Rivers
notes: Fort Defiance (1794) is listed on the NRHP (listed 1980) — NRHP designation not in vocabulary constants; designation left blank. Also known as 'Fort Defiance Park' and 'Old Fort Defiance Park'. Adjacent to Pontiac Metro Park at same confluence — distinct sites. NCT/Buckeye Trail routes through or adjacent to this area.

name: Thoreau Wildlife Reserve
governance: Diehl Family Foundation
description: 250-acre wildlife reserve encompassing various ecosystems including wetlands, prairie, hardwood forest, and old growth forest. Features interpretive signage with quotations from naturalist H.D. Thoreau. An Audubon Sanctuary Program partner supporting nesting bluebirds, wood ducks, and mallard ducks.
